title: America Must Let Go of the Middle East
gist: A truncated teaser arguing the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is an unnecessary disaster that should trigger a long-overdue American withdrawal from the Middle East, citing at least 1,700 Iranian civilian deaths, 18 U.S. troops killed and 600-plus injured, and a global energy price spike from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The body of the argument is behind a paywall cutoff, so only the opening casualty and cost accounting is extractable.

themes.theme: War costs and the Hormuz energy shock

insights.claim: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war produced a spike in energy prices whose effects are still being felt worldwide as of early August 2026.
insights.speaker: Michael Fuchs
insights.so_what: Hormuz closure is confirmed as realized, not hypothetical — the energy risk premium is being driven by an actual chokepoint shutdown rather than a threat.
insights.quote: people around the world are still reeling from the spike in energy prices caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz
insights.locator: Iran’s retaliation has killed 18 U.S. troops

insights.claim: Iranian retaliation has killed 18 U.S. troops and injured more than 600 on bases in countries neighboring Iran, meaning U.S. forward-deployed forces in the Gulf are absorbing sustained casualties.
insights.speaker: Michael Fuchs
insights.so_what: Casualty accumulation on host-nation bases raises the political cost of continued forward posture and pressures Gulf states hosting them.
insights.quote: Iran’s retaliation has killed 18 U.S. troops and injured more than 600 on bases in neighboring countries
insights.locator: Iran’s retaliation has killed 18 U.S. troops

insights.claim: The campaign has killed at least 1,700 Iranian civilians including 307 children and caused widespread damage to civilian infrastructure, which the author characterizes as a violation of international law.
insights.speaker: Michael Fuchs
insights.so_what: Civilian-casualty scale of this magnitude is the raw material for international legal and diplomatic blowback against Washington and Jerusalem.
insights.quote: killed at least 1,700 Iranian civilians (including 307 children)
insights.locator: The war with Iran is an epic disaster.

themes.theme: Case for U.S. withdrawal from the region

insights.claim: The author, a former Biden White House and Obama State Department official now at the Open Society Foundations, argues flatly that the U.S.-Israeli campaign against Iran was unnecessary and constitutes an epic disaster.
insights.speaker: Michael Fuchs
insights.so_what: Signals that the Democratic foreign-policy establishment is consolidating around retrenchment rather than course-correction, which shapes the posture of any successor administration.
insights.quote: The war with Iran is an epic disaster.
insights.locator: The war with Iran is an epic disaster.

insights.claim: The war is framed as the latest consequence of a 35-year arc of U.S. policy choices rather than a discrete decision by one administration, implying the argued remedy is structural withdrawal rather than tactical adjustment.
insights.speaker: Michael Fuchs
insights.so_what: Positions the retrenchment case as bipartisan-indicting, which broadens its potential political constituency beyond opposition to the current administration.
insights.locator: This war is the latest consequence of a series
